summary: All 23 criteria PASS (verdict PASS; threshold is all-1-weight). Because the fixture is a post-PHASE-5 end state, criteria 1-17 were re-derived by replaying the full lifecycle myself in a scratch copy (link -> remove skill-a -> re-add + link), then re-confirmed against the untouched fixture, which matches my replay on every path and sha256. Caveats a reader should know: (1) THE TREE WAS NOT CLEAN during verification — `git status --porcelain` reported ` M TESTING.md` and ` M packages/lythoskill-arena/skill/references/reproduce-sh-bdd-contract.md` (both docs, 24 insertions), plus an untracked cortex task card TASK-20260910152029904, all written by a concurrent session mid-judging; `git status --porcelain -- packages/lythoskill-deck` is empty and cli.ts diffs clean against HEAD, so the claims hold under 30cda3b62c5fbb11227f01d312cbf3f7e530441a. (2) Not covered by any criterion, and worth knowing: a hand-made symlink placed in a fan-out dir that points into THIS deck's own cold pool (name `rogue-handmade`) was silently deleted on the next link with no advisory — the rule 'symlink into its cold pool = provably created' has a false-positive surface, since the check is target-based, not provenance-based. (3) `deck remove` rewrites the TOML via parse/stringify and destroys ALL comments (top-of-file, inline `# budget`, section comments) and normalizes spacing to `[ ".agents/skills", ".kimi/skills" ]`. No criterion covers this; the fixture TOML happens to contain no comments, and the task agent's decision log called the rewrite 'cosmetic only, no semantic change, no action needed' without noting the comment loss. (4) Behaviour not named by any criterion but verified good: link is idempotent (second run byte-identical stdout and stderr, diff empty), the ownership advisory and preservation generalize to all three targets including the working_set `.claude/skills`, and `remove` also respects the boundary (foreign entries survived a remove of skill-b while skill-b was dropped from all 3 targets).
